questions.question_text: Under 174-1-17.1, which set of items must appear in a WV licensee's advertisement of a property?
questions.correct_answer: Company name, responsible broker's name with "Broker," office address, and a phone number
distractors: The responsible broker's name and nothing more
The licensee's name and WVREC license number
The property's tax parcel number and assessed value
questions.explanation: 174-1-17.1 requires each advertisement of property or a specific service to include four things: the company name, the name of the responsible broker together with the term "Broker," the physical address of a licensed office location, and a phone number. Those first three items must be displayed at no less than half the size of any associate broker, salesperson or team name in the ad. Yard signs are excused from the physical address requirement.

questions.question_text: A WV salesperson places a social media ad promoting a listing. What broker-related requirement applies?
questions.correct_answer: The ad must include the broker's name
distractors: Social media ads are exempt from broker rules
Only the salesperson's name is needed
The broker must personally approve the ad text
questions.explanation: Social media is advertising (174-1-2.1) and carries the full 174-1-17.1 element set, including the responsible broker's name with the term "Broker." 174-1-17.2 forbids a salesperson from advertising any property under their own name without the responsible broker's name. 174-1-17.4 adds a placement rule: the required information must appear on the home page or first screen the viewer sees, and must be reachable within no more than two mouse clicks when advertising on social media.

questions.question_text: A real estate team in WV wants to advertise under their team name. What additional information must be included?
questions.correct_answer: The full broker identification plus at least one named licensee team member
distractors: The team leader's license number only
No additional information is needed
The WVREC's contact information
questions.explanation: A team ad must carry the standard 174-1-17.1 elements — company name, responsible broker's name with "Broker," office address, phone — and under 17.1.a must also name at least one associate broker or salesperson who is a team member, with the term "Associate Broker" or "Salesperson" as it appears on that person's license. Under 17.1.b, any team member without a current valid license whose name appears must be identified as "Non-Licensed." It need not name every team member.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered 'advertising' under WV real estate rules?
distractors: Only newspaper and magazine ads
Only online and social media posts
Only yard signs and billboards
questions.explanation: 174-1-2.1 defines advertising as "print media, yard signs, billboards, radio, television, internet, social media, or any other advertising medium utilized by anyone engaged or employed by a brokerage." Business cards and other promotional items are handled separately by 174-1-17.3: because they do not advertise a specific property or service, they must include the licensee name, company name, and contact information.

questions.question_text: A salesperson creates a personal website promoting their real estate services. What must be included?
distractors: Only the salesperson's own name
The WVREC website address
A disclaimer that they are not a broker
questions.explanation: A personal site promoting real estate services is advertising and must carry the responsible broker's name (174-1-17.2) along with the rest of the 174-1-17.1 elements. 174-1-17.4 governs placement: the required information must appear on the home page or the first screen the viewer sees, and on social media it must be no more than two mouse clicks away.

questions.question_text: What is a 'blind ad' in WV real estate?
distractors: An ad placed by an anonymous buyer
An ad that hides the property address
An ad with intentionally wrong pricing
questions.explanation: "Blind ad" is the industry term for an advertisement that hides who is behind it; the phrase itself does not appear in West Virginia's statute or rules. The operative prohibition is 174-1-17.2: "No salesperson, associate broker, or team shall advertise any property under his, her, or their own name without the name of the responsible broker." Misleading or false advertising is separately a disciplinary ground under §30-40-19(a)(5).

questions.question_text: A WV salesperson posts a property listing online without including any brokerage name, making it appear as a for-sale-by-owner listing. What violation has occurred?
questions.correct_answer: Both a blind ad and implying independence
distractors: No violation if the seller authorized the post
Only a minor technical violation
A violation only if the property sells
questions.explanation: Both problems flow from 174-1-17.2: the ad omits the responsible broker's name, and all advertising by a salesperson must be under the direct supervision of and in the name of the responsible broker. The seller's authorization is irrelevant — it cannot waive the broker-identification rule. (Different result if the licensee owned the property: 174-1-17.5 gives an owner-licensee all the rights of an unlicensed person as to that property.)

questions.question_text: A WV licensee advertises a property for sale without obtaining the owner's authorization. What type of violation is this?
distractors: Acceptable if the property is publicly listed
Only a violation if the ad is inaccurate
A violation only for commercial properties
questions.explanation: §30-40-19(a)(10) makes it a disciplinary ground to advertise or display a "for sale," "for rent" or similar sign on any property "without an agency relationship being established or without the owner's knowledge and written consent" — note that written consent is required, not merely verbal permission. §30-40-19(a)(11) separately prohibits advertising any property on terms other than those authorized by the owner.

questions.question_text: A WV salesperson's ad implies they operate their own brokerage when they actually work under a broker. Which rule does this violate?
questions.correct_answer: Prohibition on implying independence from a broker
distractors: The first renewal CE exemption rule
The trust account notification requirement
The commission composition statute
questions.explanation: Advertising in a manner that implies the licensee is independent rather than associated with a broker is a prohibited practice. Salespersons must clearly identify their employing broker.

questions.question_text: Which advertising practice is specifically prohibited under WV real estate law?
distractors: Using the salesperson's photo in ads
Advertising on multiple online platforms
Including the property's assessed value
questions.explanation: §30-40-19(a)(5) makes the use of "misleading or false advertising" a ground for discipline, and (a)(4) reaches a course of misrepresentation or false promises made "through agents or any medium of advertising or otherwise." Photos, multi-platform campaigns and assessed values are all permissible so long as the ad is accurate and carries the required broker identification.
